outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$,
\[
0\le \sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt n
=\frac{(n+1)-n}{\sqrt{n+1}+\sqrt n}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n+1}+\sqrt n}.
\]
As $n\to\infty$, the denominator tends to infinity, so the fraction tends to $0$. Therefore,
\[
\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt n\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{proof}

outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Let $a_n=\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt n$. For all sufficiently large $n$ (indeed, for $n\ge1$),
\[
0\le a_n
=\frac{(n+1)-n}{\sqrt{n+1}+\sqrt n}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n+1}+\sqrt n}
\le \frac{1}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
The bound $1/(2\sqrt n)$ converges to $0$. Hence, by the squeeze theorem,
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=0,
\]
which is exactly
\[
\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt n\longrightarrow0.
\]
\end{proof}
